gap: No result ChatGPT got states that OutdoorGearLab tested Renogy's 100 W hard-frame foldable suitcase (the panel Renogy sells in a kit with a charge controller) and measured an average of only 49.7 W in direct sun, with peaks near 70 W and 60 Wh in one hour. That is about half its 100 W rating.
standout_why: ChatGPT's 13 results are all Renogy pages (product URL variants, the US manual PDF, the 400 W and 300 W suitcase pages) plus one Outbound Power reseller listing. They are maker or reseller spec pages, and none of them is a third-party test. I could not open them to check: renogy.com and outboundpower.com returned HTTP 429 to every request today. Its answer also gives no measured output for any card (Renogy 100 W, Renogy 200 W, ACOPOWER PLK, VEVOR 200 W). OutdoorGearLab's numbers are new, but they don't decide the pick on their own. The tested 100 W unit is from 2023 and may be the older version of today's N-Type kit, and no named lab has tested the 200 W PWM kit, the ACOPOWER or the VEVOR.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's advice to buy 200 W rather than 100 W. On a clear day at 5,000 ft, OutdoorGearLab measured an average of 49.7 W from the 100 W suitcase. A buyer charging a 12 V battery should plan on about half the label rating from the 100 W kit. In OutdoorGearLab's 2026 test of 200 W-class panels, the best result was 193 W and the worst was 112 W (56%), so the brand matters as much as the wattage. The only panel tested from ChatGPT's brands is Renogy's controller-less 200 W Portable, which made 177 W. Nothing is measured for the ACOPOWER PLK or the VEVOR 200 W with its 30 A PWM controller, so their output claims rest on the makers' word alone.

findings.source_title: The 12 Best Portable Solar Panels – OutdoorGearLab
findings.note: Updated 2026-07-13 by Sam Schild; Kenji Mowrey was lead tester. 6,300 ft, clear sky, 55–65 °F. Each panel charged a Jackery 1000 (1,070 Wh) for 2 h, with input logged every 30 min, all at the same time. The page never mentions charge controllers. The highest measured figure is 182 W (JJN Bifacial 200W, 91%), but by percentage of rating EcoFlow's 193 W of 220 W ties several others at 88%.
